references.text: The spies give their first report about the land, which forms the background for the negative report in verse 32.
Refers to the evil report (דִּבָּה) that the spies spread about the land, and God's judgment on them.
Moses recounts how the people became discouraged because of the spies' report about large people in the land.
The continuation of the negative report, where the spies describe the giants (sons of Anak) they saw.
Ezekiel uses the same expression 'a land that devours its inhabitants' (אֹכֶלֶת יוֹשְׁבֶיהָ) in connection with Israel's land.
Prohibition against spreading rumors (רָכִיל), relevant to the spies' malicious report (דִּבָּה).
The psalmist reminds how Israel despised the glorious land and did not believe God's word.
Hebrews refers to those who were not allowed to enter rest because of unbelief, which includes the spies' negative report.
